paper.title: Solving Bernoulli Rank-One Bandits with Unimodal Thompson Sampling

unmapped: the learner knows the undirected graph G with respect to which the mean vector is unimodal (increasing path from every arm to the unique optimal arm)
settings.definition_quote: A bandit instance is unimodal with respect to an undirected graph $G=(E,V)$ if its vector of means $\bm\mu = (\mu_k)_{k \in V}$ is unimodal with respect to $G$ ... In a unimodal bandit problem, the learner knows the graph G (hence the neighborhoods $\cN(k), \cN^+(k)$ for all $k\in V$), but not its parameters $\bm\mu$

unmapped: K x L arms (i,j) with Bernoulli means mu_{(i,j)} = u_i v_j (rank-one mean matrix); the learner knows this structure
u > 0 or v > 0 (entrywise), required for the unimodal structure
settings.definition_quote: this model is parameterized by two nonzero vectors $\bm u = (u_1,u_2,..u_K) \in [0,1]^K$ and $\bm v = (v_1,v_2,..v_L) \in [0,1]^L$. There are $K \times L$ arms, indexed by $(i,j) \in [K]\times[L]$ ... Each arm $(i,j)$ is associated with a Bernoulli distribution with mean $\mu_{(i,j)} :=u_i v_j$.

symbols.C_G: sum over neighbours k of the optimal arm in G of (mu_star - mu_k)/kl(mu_k, mu_star)
symbols.C_mu: constant C(mu, gamma, eps) depending on the instance, gamma and eps but not on T

conditions: mean vector is unimodal with respect to the known graph G

source.label: theo_ub_uts
source.quote: Let $\bm\mu$ be a graphical unimodal bandit instance with respect to a graph $G$. For all $\gamma \geq 2$, UTS with parameter $\gamma$ satisfies, for every $\epsilon > 0$, $$\mathcal{R}_{\bm\mu}(T,\uts(\gamma)) \leq (1+\epsilon)\sum_{k \in \cN(k_\star)}  \frac{(\mu_\star - \mu_k)}{\kl(\mu_k,\mu_\star)}\ln(T) + C(\bm\mu,\gamma,\epsilon),$$

results.notes: Regret is defined through means, so this is pseudo-regret. For rank-one bandits (graph G_1), the neighbourhood of the optimal arm is its row and column, so the bound matches Proposition 1.

symbols.C_G: sum over neighbours k of the optimal arm in G of (mu_star - mu_k)/kl(mu_k, mu_star)

conditions: mean vector is unimodal with respect to the known graph G

source.label: theo_ub_uts
source.quote: A consequence of this finite-time bound is that, for every parameter $\gamma \geq 2$, \[\limsup_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\bm\mu}(T,\uts(\gamma))}{\ln(T)} \leq \sum_{k \in \cN(k_\star)}  \frac{(\mu_\star - \mu_k)}{\kl(\mu_k,\mu_\star)},\]

results.notes: This is stated in the text as a consequence of Theorem 5. It matches the unimodal lower bound (Proposition 4) and, for rank-one bandits, the lower bound of Proposition 1.

cited_results.cited_title: Bernoulli rank-1 bandits for click feedback
cited_results.setting_description: Bernoulli rank-one bandits (K x L arms with means u_i v_j), unique optimal arm; holds for uniformly efficient algorithms. C_rank1 = sum_{i != i*} (mu_{i*,j*} - mu_{i,j*})/kl(mu_{i,j*}, mu_{i*,j*}) + sum_{j != j*} (mu_{i*,j*} - mu_{i*,j})/kl(mu_{i*,j}, mu_{i*,j*})

cited_results.setting_description: Bernoulli graphical unimodal bandits with a known graph G; holds for uniformly efficient algorithms. C_G = sum_{k in N_G(k*)} (mu_{k*} - mu_k)/kl(mu_k, mu_{k*})
